g.title: AttackLifecycle
g.text: ROUGE SNAKE | Proposed enemy attack lifecycle
Design discussion • 2026-10-27 • Not a diagram of implemented wind-up code

g.title: cluster_enemy
g.text: ENEMY • Owns decisions, attack timing and movement

g.title: cluster_view
g.text: PRESENTATION • Reads state; never applies damage

g.title: cluster_effects
g.text: GAMEPLAY EFFECTS • Game coordinates; Snake owns HP response

g.title: update
g.text: Advance attack state in fixed updates

g.title: timing
g.text: Progress phases independently of rendered frames
Release when time reaches / crosses effect time
A flag prevents duplicate effects across updates

g.title: begin
g.text: Choose attack; store target cell / direction

g.title: windup
g.text: Step back / raise weapon / draw bow

g.title: targeting
g.text: Lock at preparation start OR track then lock at release
Store coordinates / direction, not a Snake-node reference
First prototype suggestion: locked cell, 0.3 s preparation

g.title: movement
g.text: Visual offset: Draw changes sprite position only
Real step or lunge: Enemy changes grid position
Validate real movement against Board terrain

g.title: next
g.text: Observe and choose the next action

g.title: cooldown
g.text: Recovery restricts behavior; cooldown gates availability
Use recovery alone initially if sufficient
Exact durations / overlap rules remain undecided

g.title: draw
g.text: Select animation frame and visual offset

g.title: examples
g.text: Melee: step back → swing → regain balance
Bow: draw bow → fire → lower bow

g.title: projectile
g.text: Game creates arrow; it travels over time
Damage occurs on collision, not at firing

g.title: collect
g.text: Game collects effects from all living enemies

g.title: death
g.text: Game checks head death after each hit

g.title: scope
g.text: No new manager or general animation framework required.
Use small Enemy helpers first; introduce virtual hooks when a second enemy needs different behavior.
Latest lifecycle proposal supersedes the earlier two-phase boolean prototype; source and design document are not changed by this diagram.
